insights.headline: Gold holds near $4,200 after Friday's broad metals rebound; US banks set for record $5B metals-trading year
insights.summary: Spot gold rose 1.5% to $4,194.36 on Friday, touching a one-week high and heading for a weekly gain of about 1.3% as bargain buying followed Wednesday's two-month low; December futures settled at $4,216.3 while COMEX silver rose above $60.60. The rally's scale showed up on Wall Street too, where analysts expect banks to earn a record $5 billion from precious-metals trading in 2026. In India, the end of banks' bullion import tax benefit and rebounding prices kept festive demand on pause.
points: Spot gold +1.5% to $4,194.36 Friday; weekly gain ~1.3%; Dec futures settled at $4,216.3.
Silver +2.4% to $60.77; platinum +3.1% to $1,685.64. COMEX silver touched $60.62 (+2.01%).
US banks on track for record $5B in 2026 metals-trading revenue; JPMorgan made ~$700M in H1.
PBOC gold buying ran to a 23rd month; WGC: record $31B Q3 ETF inflows, 4,256 tonnes holdings.
India: bank bullion-import tax benefit withdrawn; festive buying paused as prices rebounded.

trending.title: Rally stalls near $4,200 ahead of CPI
trending.summary: Gold's rebound from a two-month low hit $4,200 resistance as elevated yields and December hike bets capped the move; next week's US inflation data decides whether it breaks higher or re-tests $4,000.

trending.title: Asia rides the metals rebound
trending.summary: COMEX and Shanghai futures rose in tandem, China's precious-metals stocks surged over 5%, and spot silver trading stayed active after the holiday on central-bank buying and record ETF inflows.

trending.title: India's festive demand stays on pause
trending.summary: With the bank import tax benefit gone and prices rebounding, dealers narrowed discounts to up to $6 an ounce and jewellers avoided fresh stocking ahead of Dussehra and Diwali.

trending.title: Banks cash in on the metals boom
trending.summary: Wall Street's precious-metals desks are on track for a record $5 billion revenue year, with JPMorgan earning about $700 million in the first half and Deutsche Bank back in bullion trading.

trending.title: Fed-hike risk still caps the rebound
trending.summary: Most FOMC policymakers expect another rate hike by year-end, and a December move remains on the table — the main cap on gold's rebound into the weekend.

items.title: Gold hits one-week high, heads for weekly gain on bargain-hunting
items.summary: Gold rose 1.5% to $4,194.36 on Friday, a second straight gain that took it to a one-week high and put it on course for a weekly rise of about 1.3%, as bargain buying followed Wednesday's two-month low. December US futures settled at $4,216.3. Reuters reports analysts see a floor near $4,000 with next week's US CPI the next catalyst; India demand stayed sluggish; silver +2.4%, platinum +3.1%.

items.title: India withdraws bank tax benefit on gold, silver, platinum imports
items.summary: India did not extend the IGST exemption for banks and state-nominated agencies importing gold, silver and platinum, so they have been paying a 3% integrated goods and services tax since April, Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava said on Thursday. The government informed the GST Council of the change, saying it puts all import routes on an equal tax footing.

items.title: Gold price holds critical $4,100 support, but can it break $4,200 as inflation risks loom?
items.summary: Analysts see initial resistance at $4,200 but optimism in prices holding above $4,100 into the weekend. Elevated yields and inflation pressure cap the upside, yet dips keep getting bought: FOREX.com's Fawad Razaqzada says the week's action suggests a bottom, while FXTM's Lukman Otunuga notes a December Fed hike remains on the table.

items.title: Futures and stocks rally together, precious metals sector surges, Western Gold hits limit up, spot silver trading sees marginal improvement [SMM Flash]
items.summary: COMEX gold rose 1.56% to $4,221.8 and COMEX silver 2.01% to $60.62 as weak US payrolls cooled October Fed-hike bets and Trump's no-strike pledge on Iran eased oil. The PBOC extended gold buying to a 23rd straight month; Russia will quintuple FX and gold purchases from Oct 7 to Nov 6. The World Gold Council reported record Q3 ETF inflows of $31B and record holdings of 4,256 tonnes.

items.title: Gold demand drops in India as prices rebound
items.summary: Gold demand in India was sluggish this week as domestic prices rebounded to about Rs 150,900 per 10 grams on Friday, after touching Rs 145,538 last week, the lowest in nearly two months. Dealers quoted discounts of up to $6 an ounce over official domestic prices, narrowing from $14 last week, as consumers paused purchases ahead of Dussehra and Diwali waiting for a correction.

items.title: US Fed Officials See Another Rate Hike Coming; Know How Indian Stocks, Rupee, Bonds And Gold Could Be Affected
items.summary: With most FOMC policymakers expecting another rate hike by year-end, the rupee faced pressure near Rs 97 to the dollar and MCX gold sat about 9.7% below its late-August peak, with COMEX gold at $4,206.60. Kotak Neo's Anindya Banerjee said a well-telegraphed 25 bps hike carries limited further downside, estimating gold could slip another 3-5% toward $3,950-4,000 an ounce if delivered.

items.title: Gold, silver prices today: Can precious metals extend recovery? Sugandha Sachdeva flags key levels
items.summary: Gold staged a comeback on Friday with MCX gold up 0.42% to Rs 1,49,735 per 10 grams and international gold futures up 1.04% to $4,200.15 an ounce, while MCX silver held near Rs 2,21,211 a kg. SS WealthStreet's Sugandha Sachdeva flagged international gold support at $4,050-4,100 an ounce and MCX gold support at Rs 1,48,000, with MCX silver support at Rs 2,17,000.

items.title: Gold, silver opened higher but remain volatile on MCX, check key levels to watch and city-wise rates
items.summary: MCX gold futures opened higher at Rs 1,49,689 per 10 grams but swung between Rs 1,48,965 and Rs 1,49,900, last trading near Rs 1,49,160; February 2026 gold held at Rs 1,51,188. December silver opened at Rs 2,23,806, touched Rs 2,24,652, then fell to Rs 2,21,367. Enrich Money's Ponmudi R flagged gold resistance at Rs 1,50,000-1,50,700 and support at Rs 1,48,000-1,47,300.

items.title: Gold steady near ₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams on MCX; silver under pressur: Key levels to watch
items.summary: MCX December gold held near Rs 1.49 lakh per 10 grams while December silver fell 1.24% to Rs 2.20 lakh a kg, pressured by a stronger dollar, US rate-hike expectations and high oil prices. Analysts cited spot gold support near $4,000 an ounce (about Rs 1.44 lakh on MCX) and silver support at Rs 2.22-2.23 lakh a kg, with the rupee at Rs 96.77 to the dollar.

items.title: Gold, silver boom puts US bank trading revenues on track for record $5 billion
items.summary: US banks are on track to earn a record $5 billion from precious-metals trading in 2026, per Crisil Coalition Greenwich data cited by the Economic Times. JPMorgan, the dominant player, made roughly $700 million in the first half, while Deutsche Bank's return to bullion trading brought in more than $200 million; Citigroup became the first new London bullion clearing member in a decade.

items.title: India's forex reserves fall by $12.95 billion to $734.61 billion in week ended Oct 2: RBI
items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell $12.95 billion to $734.61 billion in the week ended October 2, driven by a $10.66 billion drop in foreign currency assets and a $2.29 billion fall in gold reserves to $106.41 billion, RBI data showed. Reserves remained $43.5 billion above end-March 2026 levels.

items.title: Frank Talk: Gold miners beat every S&P 500 sector in Q3 despite September selloff
items.summary: Gold mining stocks, measured by the NYSE Arca Gold Miners Index, returned 17.4% in the third quarter, beating every S&P 500 sector including energy at 17.2%, while the S&P 500 itself returned 2.3%. September was rough as gold fell 6.3% on Fed rate hikes and rising real yields, though Frank Holmes cited central-bank buying, $3.8B of September ETF inflows and resilient China and India demand.
